key_insight: IQFEM reformulates immersed-boundary finite element Poisson problems into a quantum-compatible sparse linear system that can be block-encoded and solved with QSVT using polylogarithmic gate overhead in the matrix size.
engineering_relevance: This provides a potential quantum route to scalable simulation of heterogeneous solid and multiphysics problems on complex geometries, especially when classical FEM cost becomes prohibitive.
method: Encode the FEM stiffness matrix as sums of diagonal polynomial matrices and shift-matrix products using LCU.
Apply a diagonal indicator matrix built from an integer-valued level-set function to handle immersed boundaries.
Solve the block-encoded linear system with QSVT and quantum arithmetic for on-the-fly geometry operations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical examples that match the predicted complexity scaling and show roughly linear convergence for immersed domains and quadratic convergence for simply connected domains.
watch_item: The approach assumes efficient quantum arithmetic, block-encoding, and fault-tolerant QSVT, so practical hardware requirements may be substantial.
paper_title: IQFEM: A quantum finite element method for heterogeneous problems with immersed boundaries
